subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by requiring a runtime untrusted-content boundary for gh-issues plus per-spawn child tool scoping, or accept prompt-level/global-policy hardening as sufficient for this workflow?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the durable fix affects security semantics, spawned-agent API shape, session-state policy inheritance, and the SECURITY.md boundary between vulnerability and hardening.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
options.body: Land or replace the open per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length limits, or equivalent runtime isolation before considering this fixed.

options.title: Accept prompt-only mitigation
options.body: Treat a narrowed prompt-policy update as sufficient defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain inside the trusted operator-granted agent boundary.

options.title: Defer for unified delegation policy
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers design a broader delegated-agent content and capability policy across skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
recommendation.body: Land or replace the open per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length limits, or equivalent runtime isolation before considering this fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across sessions_spawn introduction, sandbox inheritance hardening, current gh-issues lines, and recent maintainer-facing review context.
